- Avoid over-optimistic forecasts in early periods following sharp price spikes; model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits persistent downward bias in 30-day forecasts, especially after mid-range price zones.
- Model underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon when recent history shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 70s to 75s).
- Model overestimates early 30-day values when recent history is flat or declining, suggesting lag in adjusting to mean reversion.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 72→67, 75→70), model fails to correct forecast early; should adjust downward by 1–2 points in next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment is absent (all 0.00), model should not assume volatility or momentum; treat as stable, low-variance regime.
- Forecast should not assume continuation of recent trend if true outcome shows divergence >3% from 3-day moving average.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 1–3 points unless sentiment indicates bullish momentum.
- In flat sentiment history, model should not forecast sharp upward moves unless recent price action shows clear breakout.
